messages.short: Stored water covers about {days}, below the 3-day minimum.
messages.partial: Stored water covers about {days}: enough for 3 days, short of the 2-week goal for staying home.

actions.short: Store about {shortByGallons} more gallons: the household uses about {water.gallonsPerDay} gallons a day (1 gallon per person{pets.waterGallonsPerDay?, plus about {pets.waterGallonsPerDay} for pets}){pets.weightsMissing?; add your pets' weights to include their water}.
actions.partial: Store about {shortByGallons} more gallons: the household uses about {water.gallonsPerDay} gallons a day (1 gallon per person{pets.waterGallonsPerDay?, plus about {pets.waterGallonsPerDay} for pets}){pets.weightsMissing?; add your pets' weights to include their water}.

notes: Pets' water (about 1 oz per lb per day, AKC) is included when their weights are recorded.

messages.short: Food covers about {days}, below the 3-day minimum.
messages.partial: Food covers about {days}: enough for 3 days, short of the 2-week goal for staying home.

actions.short: Add about {shortBy} more of non-perishable food that needs no cooking.
actions.partial: Add about {shortBy} more of non-perishable food that needs no cooking.

notes: 3-day minimum: FEMA basic kit. 2-week goal: Red Cross stay-at-home kit (no current federal page found).

finding: A well pump stops without power, so tap water stops in an outage.
action: Store more water, or plan backup power that can run the pump safely.

messages.short: Pet food covers about {days}, below the 3-day minimum.
messages.partial: Pet food covers about {days}: enough for 3 days, short of the 2-week goal for staying home.

actions.short: Add about {shortBy} more of pet food, and water for them too.{pets.kcalPerDay? Your pets need about {pets.kcalPerDay} kcal a day; check the food bag's calories per cup to convert.}
actions.partial: Add about {shortBy} more of pet food, and water for them too.{pets.kcalPerDay? Your pets need about {pets.kcalPerDay} kcal a day; check the food bag's calories per cup to convert.}

notes: Ready.gov says several days of pet food; the 3-day and 2-week thresholds mirror the human guidance. No authoritative pet-specific figure found.

finding: Many emergency shelters don't accept pets.
action: Find pet-friendly shelters, hotels or friends along your evacuation route.

messages.short: {person.label}: {need.label}: about {days} on hand, below the recommended 7 to 10.

actions.unknown: Count how many days of this medication you have.
actions.short: Ask the pharmacist or prescriber about an emergency supply or an early refill.

notes: CDC: 7 to 10 days. Needs D6 medical review.

finding: {person.label}: {need.label}: no cooler recorded to keep it cold without power.
action: Keep a cooler and ice packs (or frozen water bottles) for medication, and a fridge thermometer.

finding: {person.label}: {need.label}: no ice packs recorded to keep it cold without power.
action: Keep ice packs (or frozen water bottles) with the cooler for medication, and a fridge thermometer.

finding: {person.label}: {need.label}: no backup power recorded.{need.kwhPerDay? It needs about {need.kwhPerDay} kWh a day.}
action: Get a battery backup sized for the device, and ask the manufacturer about battery options.

finding: {person.label}: {need.label}: backup power is recorded; add its battery capacity (Wh) and the device's watts to work out how many hours it runs.{need.kwhPerDay? It needs about {need.kwhPerDay} kWh a day.}
action: Check your backup's capacity in watt-hours against the device, and test it under load.

finding: {person.label}: {need.label}: power companies can't restore power faster for one home, but many keep a list of customers who rely on medical equipment.
action: Ask your power company about its medical-needs program, and plan where to go if an outage lasts longer than the battery.

finding: {person.label}: {need.label}, in a {home.floors}-floor home.
action: Plan where they sleep and how they get out quickly, and who helps.

finding: Fuel-burning appliances or a generator, but no battery carbon monoxide detector recorded.
action: Install battery or battery-backup carbon monoxide detectors near sleeping areas.

finding: No smoke detectors recorded.
action: Install and test smoke detectors on every floor.

items.weather-radio: a battery or hand-crank radio with NOAA weather alerts
items.sanitation: moist towelettes, garbage bags and ties
items.utility-tools: a wrench or pliers to turn off utilities
items.power-bank: phone chargers and a backup battery

finding: Missing {missingCount} of {total} basic kit items: {missingList}.
action: Add {missingList}.

finding: No sleeping bag or warm blanket recorded for each person, for a cold outage.
action: Keep a sleeping bag or warm blanket for each person.

finding: No copies of important documents recorded, and this emergency may mean leaving quickly.
action: Keep copies of IDs, insurance and medical information in a go-bag or secure cloud storage.

finding: No way to treat water recorded.
action: Keep unscented bleach or purification tablets, and learn how to use them.

finding: In very hot weather water needs can double; at 2 gallons per person per day your water covers about {water.daysHotWeather}.
action: Store extra water for the heat: plan on up to 2 gallons per person per day.

finding: Pregnant or nursing people, and an infant's formula, need more water than the 1-gallon baseline.
action: Store extra water beyond 1 gallon per person per day for them.

finding: Infant in the household: no ready-to-feed formula recorded. If you formula-feed, it's the safest choice because it needs no water.
action: If you formula-feed, keep ready-to-feed formula, bottles, diapers and wipes.

finding: {person.label}: {need.label}: how long it can stay unrefrigerated depends on the product (insulin vials: up to 28 days at 59 to 86 °F).
action: Check the label or ask the pharmacist how long it lasts unrefrigerated, and note when it was last kept cold.

finding: Someone relies on medication: a written list of prescriptions and doses helps get a refill away from home.
action: Keep an up-to-date list of all prescriptions and doses with your kit.

finding: A portable generator must run outdoors at least 20 feet from windows, doors and vents; no long outdoor extension cord recorded.
action: Get a heavy-duty outdoor extension cord over 20 feet long, and pick a dry spot at least 20 feet from the house.

finding: No hand sanitizer recorded for when soap and water run short.
action: Keep soap, and hand sanitizer with at least 60% alcohol.

finding: Flood water is deceptive: 6 inches of moving water can knock an adult down and 12 inches can carry away most cars.
action: Plan an evacuation route that avoids low roads and crossings, and agree that no one drives or walks through flood water.

finding: In an earthquake, Drop, Cover and Hold On; don't run outside or stand in a doorway.
action: Practice Drop, Cover and Hold On with everyone, and agree where to meet outside after the shaking stops.

finding: Smoke: a closed-off room with a portable air cleaner is the most effective protection; no air cleaner recorded.
action: Pick a room you can close off from outside air, get a portable air cleaner sized for it, and keep NIOSH N95 respirators for going outside.

finding: {person.label}: {need.label}: the recorded battery runs it for only about {need.backupHours} hours.
action: Plan more battery capacity or a way to recharge (car, solar, generator outdoors), and decide early where to go if the outage outlasts the battery.

finding: {person.label}: {need.label}: the recorded battery runs it for about {need.backupHours} hours.
action: Plan how to recharge the battery if the outage lasts longer than that.

finding: {person.label}: {need.label}: power draw not recorded (typical: a CPAP about 56 W, a home oxygen concentrator about 350 W).
action: Find the watts on the device's label or manual and record them, so backup runtime can be worked out.

finding: The household needs about {household.kcalPerDay} kcal a day: about {household.kcal3Days} for 3 days and {household.kcal14Days} for 2 weeks{pets.kcalPerDay?, plus about {pets.kcalPerDay} kcal a day for the pets}.
action: Check your stored food's calorie labels against this, and favor calorie-dense foods that need no cooking.

finding: A dog or cat has no weight recorded, so its food and water can't be worked out.
action: Add each dog's and cat's weight in the household setup.

finding: If toilets can't flush (sewer or water failure, flooding, an earthquake, or a well pump without power), you'll need an emergency toilet; none recorded.
action: Make a twin-bucket toilet kit: two 5-gallon buckets with lids, 3–5 mil bags, sawdust or shredded paper, gloves and hand sanitizer.

finding: Tornadoes give little warning, and hurricanes can spawn them far inland.
action: Pick your shelter spot now: a basement or a small interior, windowless room on the lowest floor. Practice getting everyone there quickly, pets included.

finding: A mobile home or RV needs a tornado plan that doesn't rely on sheltering inside it.
action: Ask local emergency management where the nearest sturdy shelter is, and how much warning you'd need to get there.
notes: Ready.gov's tornado page doesn't address mobile homes; NWS guidance on mobile homes still to research.

finding: Inland, rain flooding now causes most US hurricane deaths, and it can last days after the storm.
action: Check whether your home is in a floodplain or evacuation zone, sign up for local emergency alerts, and plan where you'd go.
